instruction: In the first slide of 9_1.pptx, insert the title 'Happy Family' with 'Microsoft JhengHei' font, and add 'We Are One' as the subtitle.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator covers all three instruction requirements: title text ('Happy Family'), title font ('Microsoft JhengHei'), and subtitle text ('We Are One').
Getter correctly reads the saved pptx file using python-pptx; postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation.
Placeholder-based extraction (idx=0 for title, idx=1 for subtitle) is the correct approach for LibreOffice Impress files.
Metric applies case-insensitive string comparison with partial credit (0.34+0.33+0.33=1.0), which is appropriate for this task.

Minor robustness concern: the font extraction loop has an unconditional 'break' inside 'for run in para.runs', meaning only the first run per paragraph is ever checked. If the first run has no font directly set (None) and later runs do, the font would be missed. However, when a user explicitly selects all text and changes the font in LibreOffice Impress, python-pptx typically records the font on each run, so the first run will have it in the expected case.
Fallback mechanism handles presentations where placeholder indices are not standard.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: In the getter, change the font extraction loop to not break unconditionally after the first run: remove the bare 'break' so all runs in a paragraph are scanned before moving to the next paragraph. This improves robustness for multi-run title text frames.
